Our Story

Founded on a conviction: storytelling can transform communities.

Virtue Literacy Africa began with a book and a settlement. It grew into a five-pillar programme built on documentation, mobile access, civic education, and the belief that every child deserves the tools to lead.

Background & Inspiration

Where we came from.

Virtue Literacy Africa is an initiative of Virtue Books, a Nairobi-based publisher committed to producing values-based, civic, and accessible books for African children. In 2024, Virtue Books published Place Called Kibera — a documentary title capturing life in one of Nairobi's largest informal settlements through first-person accounts and photography.

That experience revealed both the depth of the literacy gap in informal settlements and the potential of storytelling as a tool for civic awakening. It also demonstrated the power of documentation: seeing a community clearly, on its own terms, before attempting to serve it.

VLA was founded to expand that social mandate — to move beyond publishing into active, on-the-ground delivery of literacy, civic education, and technology access in the communities that need them most.

About Place Called Kibera

The book that started it all

Place Called Kibera (Virtue Books, 2024) is a first-person narrative and photo documentary of life in Nairobi's Kibera informal settlement. It remains the foundation of VLA's commitment to documentation as the first act of civic literacy — and the first of what will become a growing library of settlement documentation titles.

The Problem

Potential, capped before a child can read.

  • /Severely limited access to books, reading materials, and enriching content.
  • /Few safe, stimulating spaces for learning and creative expression.
  • /Little exposure to values-based education that builds character and resilience.
  • /Near-total absence of civic education — no sense of rights, or the power to use them.
  • /Growing disconnect between children and the communities that will one day rely on them to lead.
  • /Rapid AI adoption threatens to deepen the digital and literacy divide unless inclusive tools are developed intentionally.

Without deliberate intervention, the cycle repeats: limited literacy leads to limited civic awareness, which leads to limited agency. Virtue Literacy Africa exists to interrupt that cycle — through books, mobile libraries, civic events, AI tools, and the young leaders who will become the most powerful agents of community transformation.

Our Foundation
Vision

An Africa where every child, regardless of where they were born, has access to books, knowledge, and the tools to shape their future.

Mission

To document Africa's informal settlement realities and respond with mobile libraries, literacy events, civic education, values-based books, and AI learning fellowships — nurturing children who are not only literate, but informed, empowered, and ready to lead.

Who We Serve

Target beneficiaries.

  • 01

    Children aged 5–17

    Children in Nairobi's informal settlements — Phase 1 focuses on Kibera, Mathare, and Korogocho.

  • 02

    Young people aged 18–28

    Particularly aspiring civic leaders and AI enthusiasts, targeted through the AI Learning Fellowships programme.

  • 03

    Caregivers, parents, and community teachers

    Adults who support children's learning at home and in informal school settings, including as primary users of the Mwangaza AI tool.

  • 04

    Persons with disabilities

    Including children and caregivers navigating accessibility barriers in education and reading materials.

Phase 1 focuses on Nairobi. Phase 2 and beyond aim to scale to other Kenyan counties and eventually across Africa.

Implementation Approach

A phased, scalable model.

Phase Timeline Geography Key Deliverables
Phase 1Foundation Year 1–2 3 Nairobi settlements: Kibera, Mathare, Korogocho 2 mobile library units; 2 new VLA books published; 3 civic education events; 1 AI fellowship cohort; Mwangaza AI pilot
Phase 2Scale Year 3–5 Additional Kenyan counties Expanded mobile library fleet; fellowship programme growth; 4 additional VLA titles; Mwangaza AI v2 with multilingual support
Phase 3Pan-African Year 5+ Pan-African Continental AI curriculum partnership; multilingual book series; diaspora fellowship track
